head: claude/exit-head-evidence-drain-9k2p1x
title: exit levers: complete the orphaned-declare surface, scope the E0 live arm to its own legs, and drain the exit-head/M20-evidence backlog class
body:
## What this is

A **backlog-drain** pass over the Tier-1 `high` rows of the exit-head / M20-evidence class in `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json`. Two structural roots fixed, one row resolved on observed evidence, one row's headline premise refuted, six advanced with a **named** blocker, one residue filed.

**No order path, no `config/strategies.yaml` value, no VM, nothing Tier-3 enacted.** All 54 relevant guards pass (`scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main`: PASS 54 / FAIL 0).

---

## Root 1 — the orphaned-declare detector was blind to the key that ARMS the exit head

`scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py --orphans-only` is the guard that catches a leg declaring an exit lever its own unit module cannot read. **MEASURED 2026-09-02** by planting declares on `ict_scalp_sol_5m`, a leg whose unit has zero exit-head code (`grep -c exit_head src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py` → 0, against 17 in `trend_donchian.py` as the positive control):

| plant | result |
|---|---|
| `exit_head_threshold` + `exit_head_action` | orphan reported, **exit 1** |
| `exit_head_model` + `exit_head_action` | **SILENT, exit 0** |

The second plant is the one that ships. `trend_donchian._exit_head_verdict` returns `None` unless `exit_head_action == "close"` and falls back to the artifact's own tau when no threshold is given — so **`exit_head_action` is the ARMING key and `exit_head_threshold` an optional modifier**, and the detector was keyed on the modifier while blind to the arm. The tuple's other entry, `"exit_head"`, is a key no leg declares and no module reads.

**Not confined to `exit_head`.** A scan of every `meta|cfg|cfg_dict.get("<prefix>...")` read across `src/units/strategies/*.py` + `src/runtime/*.py` found the same incompleteness in **3 of 4** mechanisms — `stale_exit_below_r` and `trail_decay_stall_bars` were missing too; only `giveback_stop` was complete. **And the table was duplicated**: `scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py::_KEYED_MECHANISMS` carried its own copy with identical staleness.

So the remedy is a **derivation**, not four hand-added strings:

- `DECLARE_KEYS` (the full config surface, used for `declared`) is now separate from `MECHANISMS` (the narrow probe for whether a module *implements* the lever — unchanged, so the family-coverage numbers do not move). Widening the first can only widen orphan detection; if it reached `module_implements`, a unit that merely mentions a key would read as able to run the lever.
- `declared_surface_gaps()` derives the surface from the implementations and the guard's `--self-test` **FAILS** on any read-but-undeclared key — it cannot silently regrow the next time a lever gains a knob.
- Kept **one-sided on purpose**: an unread key in the table only widens detection, so making that an error too would have required an exception mechanism for `"exit_head"` — and an exception mechanism is how a guard becomes cheaper to lie to than to satisfy.
- `exit_path_coverage.py` now imports both tables instead of restating them.

**Verified:** live config still reports **zero** orphans (no false positive); the previously-silent plant now exits 1; the self-test carries a positive control that removing `exit_head_action` from the table *is* detected as a gap.

## Root 2 — the E0 live arm loaded the whole journal instead of its own legs

`build_exit_head_dataset.py --db` pulled every strategy-attributed closed trade and `family_of()` buckets on the strategy **NAME**, so a scalp round inhaled same-symbol siblings and invented families it never asked for. Measured 2026-08-13 (relays #8854/#8855): `donchian {live: 3}, pullback {live: 6}` beside `ict_scalp_xrp_15m {harness: 353}` — the graded leg's own live count was **ZERO** — and those 0-harness families then crashed training.

`--legs` now scopes the live arm, and the round driver passes it on the same line it passes `--db` so the two cannot drift.

- `legs_filter_state` is three values, **not collapsed**: `not_requested` / `applied` / `applied_no_match`. "We did not scope" and "we scoped and the journal holds nothing" are opposite statements, and reading the second as the first is how an empty live arm gets blamed on data accrual (which is what happened on 2026-08-12).
- `legs_dropped` names the excluded strategies and their counts, so the pull stays **visible** rather than merely prevented.
- `rows_matching_filters` keeps its pre-existing meaning, so a reader comparing it across rounds is not handed a different population under the same key.

Tests run against a **real** sqlite journal, including the positive control that the *unscoped* load does still pull the sibling — without which the scoped test proves nothing.

---

## Backlog dispositions

**RESOLVED (1)** — `BL-20260815-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-MATRIX-DISAGREES-WITH-THE-4-ARM-SCREEN`. Both conjuncts of criterion (b) read out of `exit-refinement-coverage.json`: the sol cell carries the partition-dependence note citing the row by id, and the operator answered the ship question (CANCELLED, 2026-08-23). **One clause verified as RECORDED rather than as SEQUENCED, and the row says so** — both facts sit in the same dated entry and I cannot establish the flip was weighed *before* the decision.

**PREMISE REFUTED (1)** — `BL-20260810-EXIT-LEVER-SPACE-UNDER-ENUMERATED` still says the operator's near-TP-reversal case has no lever anywhere. **It does.** `--rr-floor` (M31 P5) is that lever — its help text is the case verbatim — and it was swept: `docs/research/e35-rr-floor-walkforward-2026-08-20.md`, 19 legs × 3 cells = 57 rows, walk-forward 2021–2026, net of fees, 2 Path-A PASS. The row's *second* clause is satisfied; what remains is the first, now narrowed to three named flags (`--rr-floor`, `--timeout-bars`, `--exit-grain`) with no matrix column and no recorded n/a.

**ADVANCED, BLOCKER NAMED (6)** — including `EDGE-SMALL-AND-INCONSISTENT`, recorded as **100% operator-blocked** so it stops consuming review slots; and `SHIPPED-DONCHIAN-1H-HEAD-RESTS-ON-BESTARM`, where I measured that the corpus carries no `selected_tau` on any of its 33 rows — so whether those rounds ran at holdout-tau code is *"we could not look"*, not *"they did not"*.

**FILED (1)** — `BL-20260902-AVAX-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-NEGATIVE-CONTRADICTED-AND-UNANSWERED`, the half of the resolved row its sol-only criterion did not cover.

## What I could NOT do, and why

- **`BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-VERDICT-DEPENDS-ON-LEG-ARGUMENT-ORDER` — deliberately not acted on.** Flipping `--total-sort` to default is a one-line change and the wrong first move: it changes recorded AUCs across the committed corpus, so the corpus must be re-measured first or the file silently mixes two non-comparable conventions with no field to tell them apart — this row's own defect, one level up. Backfilling a `legs` field onto the existing 33 rows is refused too: the order those runs used is not recoverable from any committed artifact, and writing one in would be fabricating provenance. The order of operations is recorded on the row.
- **No trainer round.** Three rows' criteria require one (`issue_write` → 403 for this session, so the `trainer-vm-diag-request` relay is unreachable from here).
- **Three operator decisions** remain and are named on their rows; none is a session's to take.
- **No matrix columns added** — a schema change to a 765 KB artifact behind four guards, with other sessions working that file; it wants its own PR.

## Note for the reviewer

`tests/test_total_sort_tie_break.py` has 5 failures **on `main` as well as here** — `train_exit_head.py` imports numpy, which is absent from this sandbox. Confirmed by stashing and re-running. Not caused by this change.
